reasoning: Verified against test/test_ducklib.py at HEAD and duckdb.h (v1.3.2 doc comments). duckdb.h is unambiguous: duckdb_query's docstring states 'after running duckdb_query, duckdb_destroy_result must be called on the result object even if the query fails' (duckdb.h:928-929), and duckdb_fetch_chunk's docstring states 'The result must be destroyed with duckdb_destroy_data_chunk' (duckdb.h:1093). aux_close_db (test_ducklib.py:67-69) only calls duckdb_disconnect and duckdb_close - no destroy_result/destroy_data_chunk call, and nothing in the C API contract implies disconnect/close frees outstanding results or chunks. Confirmed each cited case: (1) test_query (132-137) obtains out_result via aux_query_1 and calls only aux_close_db - no duckdb_destroy_result. (2) test_duckdb_column_count_and_duckdb_row_count (153-160) same pattern - no destroy_result. (3) test_duckdb_fetch_chunk_exhausted (212-219) calls duckdb_fetch_chunk twice into the same local chunk_p (line 215 then 217), so the first chunk handle is overwritten/lost before any destroy could be issued, and out_result is never destroyed either - both leaked. (4) The three aux_get_data_vector consumers - test_duckdb_data_chunk_get_column_count (185-189), test_duckdb_data_chunk_get_size (192-196), and test_duckdb_fetch_chunk_data_chunk_get_vector_get_data_vector (222-235) - each receive data_chunk_p from aux_get_data_vector and call only aux_close_db, never duckdb_destroy_data_chunk on the chunk (nor destroy_result on the underlying result). This is a real contrast with the surrounding tests that do call the destroy path correctly, e.g. test_query_invalid_sql:149, test_duckdb_destroy_result:168, test_duckdb_destroy_data_chunk:207, test_execute_prepared:333 - confirming the omission in the cited tests is inconsistent with the file's own established pattern, not an intentional/alternate teardown route. Severity of medium is appropriate: these are per-test resource leaks in test code (not a production defect), harmless to correctness since the process exits and OS reclaims memory, but they are real DuckDB-owned C allocations that outlive their scope and - as the reviewer notes - mean these specific tests never exercise the destroy/teardown path, weakening their ability to catch a real leak regression in the bindings.
notes: TST-MEM-1 (a related finding) covers a distinct issue in the same code region (aux_get_data_vector discarding the out_result numpy buffer itself, making destroy_result structurally impossible); TST-MEM-2 additionally/separately flags the fetched-chunk leak in those same consumer tests plus two unrelated tests (test_query, test_duckdb_column_count_and_duckdb_row_count) and the double-leak in test_duckdb_fetch_chunk_exhausted. The two findings overlap in which tests they touch but describe different missing destroy calls (result-buffer vs. chunk-handle vs. plain result); no duplication of the core claim.
